lane: A3 (outcome-blind proposal lane, FOREX-FREE-V1 F4, session-flow perspective)
mechanism_name: London-Open Session Continuation: 3-bar post-open momentum, flattened strictly before the NY rollover
economic_mechanism: At the London open (08:00 Europe/London) the largest FX liquidity pool of the day arrives: the UK is the largest global FX dealing centre at 38% of global turnover (BIS Triennial Survey 2022, confirmed via Bank of England/BIS releases). Overnight (Asian-session) information and unexecuted order flow are repriced when London dealers, clients and algorithms arrive. The signed return of the first three completed London-session H1 bars measures the direction of this arrival flow. Intraday-momentum literature shows early-session returns predict late-session continuation: Gao, Han, Li & Zhou (2018, JFE) in equity futures (first half-hour predicts last half-hour), with follow-up evidence across currency futures, and Elaut, Lampaert & Froemmel (2018, J. Financial Markets) documenting intraday momentum in a session-traded FX market, attributing it to liquidity provision rather than informed trading. Candidate frictions that carry the effect through the day: slow hedging by dealers, stop-loss order cascades executing in the direction of the move (Osler 2003/2005), and liquidity-provision inventory that is unwound gradually rather than instantly. The position is held only inside the same trading day and is always flattened at the last completed H1 bar strictly before the 17:00 America/New_York rollover, so the strategy earns no financing and carries no overnight risk by construction.
expected_counterparty: Counterparties taking the other side of the post-open continuation: (i) Asian-session limit orders and thin-liquidity market makers whose quotes are consumed when London liquidity arrives; (ii) stop-loss orders triggered by the post-open move, which execute as market orders in the direction of the move (mandated risk management, price-insensitive; Osler 2003/2005); (iii) late intraday hedgers who adjust hedge ratios with a lag. These counterparties tolerate the loss because their trades are mandate-, hedge- or stop-driven rather than speculative profit-seeking.
signal_fields_and_publication_clock: Inputs per pair: Twelve Data H1 OHLC bar closes and bar open timestamps (UTC) only; session boundary instants from the frozen calendar (computed via zoneinfo named zones, never from data, never from fixed offsets). A bar timestamped T (bar open) is COMPLETED at T+1h and only completed bars may enter any signal. Signal timeline (London open L = 08:00 Europe/London on weekday d): c0 = close of the last completed bar with end <= L (the bar [L-1h, L) London); c3 = close of the 3rd London-session bar (bar [L+2h, L+3h) London), publicly determinable at instant L+3h = 11:00 London; momentum score m = c3/c0 - 1. All signal information is therefore public no later than 11:00 London on day d; no future bar is touched. London's UTC offset is always a whole hour (+0/+1), so L always coincides with an H1 bar boundary - implementation must assert this alignment and fail closed if violated.
entry_exit_and_rollover_flat_rule: Entry: if m > 0, position +1 (long base currency); if m < 0, position -1; if m = 0, no trade. Fill at the close of the NEXT completed H1 bar after the signal bar (bar [L+3h, L+4h) London; fill instant L+4h = 12:00 London). Exit (flatten): at the close of the last completed H1 bar whose end is STRICTLY BEFORE the same weekday's NY rollover instant R = 17:00 America/New_York. Because hourly bars end on whole hours, this is the bar ending at 16:00 New York wall clock in both EST and EDT (winter: bar ends 21:00Z < 22:00Z rollover; summer: bar ends 20:00Z < 21:00Z rollover), so the DST rule is uniform and exact. Holding window is uniformly 9 completed bars (12:00 London -> 16:00 New York wall clock). Friday: the last in-session bar IS the 16:00 New York weekly-close bar, so the flatten rule coincides with the frozen Friday 16:00 America/New_York week close and never spans the weekend. One position per pair per day; no re-entry. Missing-bar rule (fail closed): if any required bar (c0, c3, entry fill bar, or flatten bar) is absent for a pair-day, that pair-day is skipped as NO_TRADE and counted; no interpolation, no carry-over of signals.
execution_model: Next-allowed-bar execution, conservative close-to-close: the signal is computed on completed bar t only; the earliest possible fill is the close of completed bar t+1 (never bar t, never intra-bar). Under the top cost-stress cell an additional one-event delay is applied (fill at bar t+2 close). No assumptions about intra-bar fills, open-of-bar fills, or fill quality beyond the frozen proxy-cost matrix.

frozen_cost_stress_matrix.basis: Conservative PROXY costs chosen a priori, not estimated from data and not evidence of achievable execution. No bid/ask series exists in the authorized contract.
frozen_cost_stress_matrix.applied_to: every fill (entry and exit), so base round trip = 3.0 bps
frozen_cost_stress_matrix.one_event_delay_definition: S3 shifts the entry fill one additional completed bar later (bar t+2 close instead of t+1 close); the flatten rule is unchanged and still executes at the last completed bar strictly before the rollover.

anchor.definition: London-open 3-bar continuation exactly as specified: position sign(c3/c0 - 1) entered at the next completed bar (12:00 London), flattened at the last completed bar strictly before 17:00 America/New_York, all 7 pairs.
anchor.why_it_validates: If London-open order-flow arrival carries intraday continuation, the anchor must show positive net expectancy on a majority of pairs at the frozen base cost, with the mechanism's predicted ordering anchor >= neighbour >= negative control.

neighbour.definition: New York-open analogue, identical construction: N = 08:00 America/New_York; c0' = last completed bar with end <= N; c3' = close of the 3rd NY-session bar (signal public at 11:00 New York wall clock); fill at next completed bar (12:00 New York); same flatten rule; same 7 pairs. Theoretically justified because the NY open is the second-largest daily liquidity event (US is the second-largest FX dealing centre; the NY/late-London overlap is the day's turnover peak), so the same arrival-repricing friction should produce the same-signed but WEAKER effect (the informational gap across the London midday is smaller than across the Asian night).
neighbour.why_it_validates: A same-signed, weaker neighbour effect shows the mechanism generalizes across liquidity events as the theory predicts (monotone in the size of the liquidity arrival), rather than being a London-bar artifact.
neighbour.why_it_destroys: If the neighbour is opposite-signed to the anchor on >= 4 of 7 pairs, the anchor effect does not generalize and is most plausibly a London-timezone/data artifact (e.g., bar-grid misalignment around BST/GMT switches), falsifying the proposal.

negative_control.definition: Sign-flipped anchor (anti-momentum): fade the 3-bar London move, identical signal timing, timing of fills, flatten rule, pair universe and frozen cost matrix.
negative_control.why_it_validates: Not a validation arm: it is the causal control. A directional order-flow mechanism only supports the proposal if flipping the sign destroys the edge.
negative_control.why_it_destroys: If the sign-flipped control matches or beats the anchor's net per-trade expectancy on >= 4 of 7 pairs at base cost, the measured effect is not causal continuation (it would indicate close-series microstructure artifacts such as stale-quote bounce or reversal structure), falsifying the proposal.

falsification_rule.preregistered: Evaluated once in F8 after scoring is authorized; thresholds frozen now, no re-tuning, no rescue.
reject_if_any: F1a (causal control): at cost cell S1, the sign-flipped negative control's mean net per-trade return >= the anchor's on >= 4 of 7 pairs.
F1b (cost stress): at cost cell S3 (x2 spread + one-event delay), the anchor's cumulative net return < 0 on >= 5 of 7 pairs.
F1c (neighbour contradiction): the NY-open neighbour's mean net per-trade return is opposite in sign to the anchor's on >= 4 of 7 pairs.

F1d (DST robustness, diagnostic on anchor trades, not a new trial): split anchor trades by whether the trade date's session instants were computed under EDT or EST. If the anchor's mean net per-trade return flips sign between the EDT and EST subsets on >= 5 of 7 pairs, the effect is a clock artifact and the proposal is rejected.
falsification_rule.necessary_survival_conditions: Anchor cumulative net return > 0 at S1 on >= 5 of 7 pairs, AND mean per-trade ordering anchor >= neighbour >= negative control holds on a majority of pairs (neighbour may be weaker but must be same-signed).
falsification_rule.no_other_analysis: No additional parameter configurations, windows, thresholds or variants may be scored for this proposal; a failed rule is terminal for the cycle.

expected_regimes: Expected to work in macro-flow regimes: data-release weeks, policy-repricing weeks, directional post-Asian-gap days, high London/NY-overlap volatility. Expected to degrade in holiday-thinned range weeks (late December, mid-August), post-central-bank-meeting consolidation, and one-sided intervention episodes (JPY, CHF) where cascades overshoot and reverse intraday.

dst_session_clock_spec.week_window: Open Sunday 21:00 America/New_York, close Friday 16:00 America/New_York (frozen calendar; identical to research/assets/forex/sessions.py DEFAULT_FX_WEEK_CONVENTION). Out-of-session bars excluded by calendar rule only.
dst_session_clock_spec.session_anchors: London session open 08:00 Europe/London; New York session open 08:00 America/New_York (declared a priori, frozen for the whole cycle, never re-optimized).
dst_session_clock_spec.rollover: 17:00 America/New_York daily; positions flattened at the last completed H1 bar with end strictly before the rollover instant (uniformly the bar ending 16:00 New York wall clock, EST and EDT alike).
dst_session_clock_spec.implementation_requirements: All instants computed in named IANA zones via zoneinfo (DST-correct); nonexistent wall times fail closed, ambiguous wall times resolved by explicit fold policy; whole-hour bar-boundary alignment asserted; no fixed UTC offsets anywhere; Sunday 21:00 New York open maps to Monday's FX trading day and contains no London/NY-session signal.

exact_trial_count.decomposition: 3 variants (anchor, NY-open neighbour, sign-flipped negative control) x 7 pairs = 21 scored trials, each evaluated once over 2020-01-29 -> 2026-09-02.
exact_trial_count.not_additional_trials: The 3-column frozen cost stress matrix re-costs the identical 21 trade streams and creates no new trials; the F1d EDT/EST split is a diagnostic re-partition of anchor trades, not a new trial.
exact_trial_count.forbidden: No parameter grid of any kind: 3 bars is the only momentum window, the London/NY anchors are the only session anchors, and no configuration outside this document may be scored.

data_fields_used.source: Twelve Data H1 OHLC, closes-eligible canonical bars only, 2020-01-29 -> 2026-09-02
data_fields_used.signal_dependency: closes and timestamps only (open/high/low unused by the signal; available if F8 implementation needs them for audit)
data_fields_used.per_pair: each pair uses only its own series; no cross-pair inputs

forbidden_assumptions_check.no_bid_ask: PASS - no bid/ask data used or assumed recoverable; the 1.5 bps/side proxy is a declared conservative stress, not a data claim, and outputs are labelled RESEARCH_CANDIDATE_NOT_LIVE_READY.
forbidden_assumptions_check.no_volume: PASS - no volume field used; centralized FX volume is forbidden under the contract.
forbidden_assumptions_check.no_financing: PASS - every position is flattened at the last completed bar strictly before the NY rollover; zero swap/financing assumed, accrued or collected.
forbidden_assumptions_check.no_overnight: PASS - no position spans a rollover instant or the weekend; the Friday flatten coincides with the frozen Friday 16:00 America/New_York week close.
forbidden_assumptions_check.no_lookahead: PASS - signals use completed bars only; fills occur at the next completed bar at the earliest.
forbidden_assumptions_check.no_outcome_tuning: PASS - zero returns/backtests computed in this lane; all constants frozen before any scoring.

literature_sources.title: Market Intraday Momentum
literature_sources.authors: Lei Gao, Yufeng Han, Sophia Zhengzi Li, Guofu Zhou
literature_sources.claim: The market's first half-hour return positively predicts its last half-hour return (equity futures); basis for testing early-session continuation and its attribution to slow hedging/inventory frictions.

literature_sources.title: Intraday Momentum in FX Markets: Disentangling Informed Trading from Liquidity Provision
literature_sources.authors: G. Elaut, C. Lampaert, M. Froemmel
literature_sources.claim: Intraday momentum exists in a session-traded FX market and is driven by liquidity provision rather than informed trading.

literature_sources.title: Stop-Loss Orders and Price Cascades in Currency Markets
literature_sources.venue: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report No. 150; published Journal of International Money and Finance 24(2), 219-241 (2005)
literature_sources.claim: Currency stop-loss orders execute in the direction of the prevailing move and generate rapid, self-reinforcing price cascades - a candidate friction sustaining intraday continuation.

literature_sources.title: OTC foreign exchange turnover in April 2022 (Triennial Central Bank Survey); UK 38% share via Bank of England release
literature_sources.authors: Bank for International Settlements; Bank of England
literature_sources.venue: BIS Triennial Survey commentary and Bank of England national results
literature_sources.claim: The UK is the largest global FX dealing centre (38% of turnover in the 2022 survey); the US is the second-largest centre - justifies London/NY session anchors.
